F16.title: 5. From foundational charts to a concrete forecast story | F16
F16.notebook_commentary_excerpt: 5. From foundational charts to a concrete forecast story F16 Andrea exported real hourly predictions for all seven of the team's model series, including the 50/50 hybrid, and ERCOT's benchmark is available on most hours. F20.title: Figure F20 — Do Rolling SARIMA and Weather XGBoost make similar mistakes?
F20.notebook_commentary_excerpt: Figure F20 — Do Rolling SARIMA and Weather XGBoost make similar mistakes? Plot signed errors (forecast minus actual) for each of the same hours. If both models make nearly identical errors, averaging offers little opportunity for cancellation. If their mistakes differ, an ensemble might improve accuracy. The correlation is an empirical diagnostic, not a guarantee of better results. The axes cross at zero, so points on opposite-sign quadrants indicate hours where one model overpredicted while the other underpredicted.

Evaluate the fixed and earlier-selected blends against both component models, on the later segment only. The small top-demand group is descriptive and should not guide direct operational model switching.

F24.title: Figure F24 — A concrete forecast case study
F24.notebook_commentary_excerpt: Figure F24 — A concrete forecast case study We return to the same July 19–25, 2026 (Central Time) week used in F10/F16, now adding the fixed blend. Looking at one high-load week can reveal how averages hide shape and timing errors, but it cannot substitute for the full evaluation.

F25.title: Figure F25 — How often does the 50/50 blend reduce forecast error?
F25.notebook_commentary_excerpt: Figure F25 — How often does the 50/50 blend reduce forecast error? This chart shows the percentage of later-period hours for which the fixed blend's absolute error is lower than Rolling SARIMA's, Weather XGBoost's, or both models' errors. These are descriptive rates, not a rule for choosing tomorrow's model. Overall MAE can improve even when the blend is not the best choice for a majority of individual hours.

F32.title: F32 | Do changes relative to average also mean useful forecasting skill?
F32.notebook_commentary_excerpt: F32 Do changes relative to average also mean useful forecasting skill? A drop below a model’s own MAE does not mean that it beats a meaningful forecasting alternative. The left panel measures improvement over the seasonal naive baseline using the period-specific MAE for both approaches; the right panel compares model error against ERCOT day-ahead on the identical hours.

F33.title: F33 | How did errors behave during a real peak week?
F33.notebook_commentary_excerpt: F33 How did errors behave during a real peak week? The previous figures average groups of hours. Here we show actual individual hourly absolute errors for the July 19–25 case study, keeping the typical MAE reference as a horizontal line. An individual large miss is not itself an MAE; MAE is the average over many such misses.
